audit.summary: The first target proves that there is a finite, connected, bipartite, 2-degenerate graph H on Fin q with ex(n,H) ≥ c·n^{3/2+ε} for all sufficiently large n, for some constants c, ε > 0. It also proves an extra property not in the paper: under every proper 2-colouring, each colour class contains a vertex of degree > 2. The second target proves the negation of a formalized Erdős degeneracy conjecture: for every r > 0 and every finite bipartite r-degenerate H, ex(n,H) = O(n^{2−1/r}). Both statements match the paper; the only deviation is the harmless extra colouring/degree conjunct, which makes Lean stronger.

glossary.plain: For a finite set s and vertex v: the set of vertices in s adjacent to v in G.
glossary.standard_concept: neighbourhood of v restricted to s

glossary.plain: Every nonempty finite vertex set s contains a vertex with at most r neighbours inside s.
glossary.note: Stated for induced subgraphs. This is equivalent to the paper's 'every nonempty subgraph has a vertex of degree ≤ r', since deleting edges only lowers degrees.

glossary.plain: For all r > 0 and all bipartite r-degenerate graphs H on Fin q, ex(n,H) = O(n^{2−1/r}) as n → ∞.
glossary.note: Uses Mathlib's extremalNumber, which matches the paper's ex(n,H). The hypothesis r > 0 avoids the 1/0 junk value.

lean_claims.plain: There exist q and a graph H on Fin q with all of the following: H is connected, bipartite and 2-degenerate; for every proper 2-colouring and each colour class, the maximum degree over that class exceeds 2; and there are reals c > 0, ε > 0 with c·n^{3/2+ε} ≤ ex(n,H) for all sufficiently large n.
There exist r > 0 and a bipartite r-degenerate graph H on Fin q such that ex(n,H) is not O(n^{2−1/r}).

paper_claims.plain: There exist a fixed connected bipartite 2-degenerate graph H and constants c, ε > 0 with ex(n,H) ≥ c·n^{3/2+ε} for all sufficiently large n.
Erdős's conjecture that every bipartite r-degenerate graph has ex(n,H) = O(n^{2−1/r}) is false (already for r = 2).
Failure of compactness (covered elsewhere, sibling file).

flags.explanation: The extra conjunct requires that, under every proper 2-colouring, each colour class contains a vertex of degree > 2. This also forces both classes to be nonempty, since sup over an empty class is 0. The paper's Theorem 1.2 does not state this, though it is presumably meant to rule out the Füredi/AKS case. It only strengthens the Lean statement.

lint_verdicts.why: This is a Finset.card of a finite filter, not Nat.card of a possibly infinite type, so no junk value arises.
The hypothesis 0 < r excludes 1/0, and (2:ℕ):ℝ = 2 exactly.
(3:ℝ)/2 is real division and equals 1.5 exactly.
